title: Model Feature Churn Index & Prospector Playbook
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem statement: As open-model availability and feature divergence accelerate, we lack a single, measurable signal that summarizes which models are changing in ways that matter to Redwood customers (latency regression, API surface changes, quantization support, license shifts, or capability drift). PMs and sourcing need an actionable, automated index and weekly prospecting workflow to prioritize scouting, procurement trials, and fallback readiness.

Objective: Build a repeatable "Model Feature Churn Index" (MFCI) and an associated Prospector Playbook that turns model-landscape telemetry into procurement triggers and research tasks. The index should be computable daily for our prioritized model universe and surface in a Console dashboard and a weekly Prospector report.

Scope & deliverables:
- MFCI definition and formula (documented, explainable): a normalized 0..1 score combining Feature Volatility, Performance Delta, Compatibility Delta, and Governance Delta (see formula sketch below).
- Ingestion pipeline for model-change signals: release notes (Hugging Face/Repos), GitHub commit metadata, public benchmark results, license/policy notices, and our internal regression evals.
- Prototype ETL and scheduler that computes MFCI for the top ~120 target models (open and third-party variants).
- Console dashboard: time-series of MFCI per model, top drivers for recent churn (e.g., "tokenization change + 12% latency increase"), model tagging, and procurement trigger badges.
- Prospector Playbook (operational): daily triage rules, weekly report format, owner roles, and procurement escalation thresholds.
- Runbook + alerting: actions for 3 trigger bands (watch, probe, escalate).

MFCI (sketch):
- Feature Volatility (FV): % of breaking API changes or new capabilities in release notes & manifest (0..1)
- Performance Delta (PD): normalized change in median latency and token-cost (0..1)
- Compatibility Delta (CD): change in quantization/hardware support & KV cache semantics (0..1)
- Governance Delta (GD): license changes, export controls, or notable security advisories (0 or 1 weighted higher)
- MFCI = weighted_sum(0.35*FV, 0.30*PD, 0.20*CD, 0.15*GD) normalized to 0..1.

Procurement trigger bands (proposal):
- Watch (MFCI >= 0.45): add to weekly Prospector stack; run focused evals on critical prompts.
- Probe (MFCI >= 0.65): instantiate a short procurement trial or reserve bench capacity; notify Solutions Eng.
- Escalate (MFCI >= 0.85): initiate procurement + security review + contract readiness checklist; alert Sales for customer-facing risk communications.

Data sources & instrumentation tasks:
- Public release feed connector (Hugging Face model metadata & RSS) — engineering ticket dependency.
- GH commit and tag crawler for model repos and tokenizer tools.
- Benchmark ingestion: our internal evals (evals job outputs) + scraped external benchmarks.
- License and legal signal feed: automated license map per model (OSS license, restrictions).
- Internal regression deltas: daily job comparing baseline prompt sets across model candidates.
- Mapping layer: canonical model IDs, variant families, and hardware affinity tags.

Stakeholders & owners:
- PM lead: Aisha Chen (owner of index definition & playbook)
- Data/Infra: Eng (owner of ingestion and scheduler) - contact: Marco Diaz (assignee)
- Applied ML: provides regression deltas and eval harnesses
- Solutions Eng & Sales: run probes and procurement trials
- Legal & Security: security & license gating for escalate band

Out-of-scope: full automation of procurement approvals, automated contract negotiation, and on-prem deployment automation. Those require separate cross-functional tickets.

Success metrics (30 days):
- Pipeline computes MFCI for 120 models daily with <5% missing data rate.
- Prospector weekly report produced automatically and consumed by 3 internal teams.
- At least one procurement probe triggered from MFCI thresholds within 6 weeks and tracked through the playbook.

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket focuses on a behavioral, explainable signal (feature churn) rather than raw capability benchmarking or price only — it intentionally blends operational compatibility and governance signals so procurement decisions are informed by both product risk and technical regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion pipeline available and documented: release/feed + GH commits + license mapping for >=120 models
Daily scheduled job produces MFCI for each model; historical series stored for >=90 days
Console dashboard prototype with model ranking, driver breakdown, and drilldowns is accessible to PMs/SEs
Prospector Playbook published in Confluence with triage rules, owner list, and example escalation for MFCI >=0.85
Alerting wired to Slack channel #model-prospector and email for escalate band
At least one end-to-end probe executed following the playbook (trial request, eval results, procurement notes)
